w:r.w:t: LaundryLink is a multi-platform laundry booking system consisting of:
• Backend REST API — Spring Boot 3.5.11 / Java 17 / PostgreSQL (via Supabase)
• Web Frontend — React 19.2.4 / TypeScript 5.7.3 / Vite 6.3.5 / Tailwind CSS 4.2.0
• Mobile App — Android (Kotlin, API 26+) / Retrofit 2.11.0 / Kotlin Coroutines
Books laundry slots, uploads files, views booking status
Manages their shop, configures slots/services, updates booking status
Superuser — manages all bookings, shops, and slot configuration

The most recent significant change prior to this regression cycle was PR #24: Vertical Slice Refactoring (commit 318a9ba), which reorganized the entire backend codebase from a layered architecture to a feature-vertical slice pattern.
├── controllers/ ← All REST controllers in one flat package
├── services/ ← All business logic in one flat package
├── repositories/ ← All data access in one flat package
├── models/ ← All JPA entities in one flat package
├── dto/ ← All DTOs in one flat package
│ ├── booking/ ← Booking + Controller + Repository + Service + QrCodeService + DTOs
│ ├── payment/ ← Payment + Controller + Repository + Service + events + DTOs
│ ├── shop/ ← Shop + Service entities + Controller + Repository + Service + DTOs
│ └── slot/ ← SlotConfig + Controller + Repository + Service + DTOs
├── user/ ← User entity + UserRepository + AuthenticatedUserService + UserRole
Easier to find relevant files per feature
Both now follow vertical slice layout
The refactoring was a structural reorganization only — no business logic was changed. However, the following risks required regression validation:
• Bean injection failures after class moves
• Spring Security configuration still applies globally
• Frontend route resolution still maps to correct feature components
│ │ ├── features/ ← Vertical slices (admin, auth, booking, owner, payment, shop, slot)
│ │ └── shared/ ← Cross-cutting concerns (config, security, user, web)
│ ├── features/ (admin, auth, booking, customer, landing, shop-owner, shops)
This regression test covers all implemented functional requirements across the three platforms (backend API, web frontend, mobile app) after the vertical slice refactoring.
• Verify no regressions were introduced by the vertical slice refactoring
• Confirm all previously working features continue to work correctly
• Confirm role-based access control is enforced
• Verify third-party integrations remain functional (PayMongo, Google OAuth, Supabase Storage)

7.1 BUG-01: File Upload Size Limit Not Enforced on Backend

The file upload endpoint (POST /api/bookings/{id}/upload) accepts files larger than the documented 10MB limit. The frontend correctly validates file size before upload and blocks oversized files on the client side, but the backend does not independently enforce the size limit. A direct API call with a file exceeding 10MB succeeds with HTTP 200 instead of returning HTTP 413 or HTTP 400.
1. Create a valid booking and obtain the booking ID.
2. Using Postman or curl, send a multipart POST to /api/bookings/{id}/upload with a file larger than 10MB.
3. Observe that the backend accepts the file and returns HTTP 200 with a file URL.
Expected Behavior: HTTP 413 Payload Too Large or HTTP 400 Bad Request.
Actual Behavior: HTTP 200 OK — file uploaded successfully to Supabase Storage.

The BookingController.java upload handler does not validate MultipartFile.getSize() before passing the file to the service layer. The 10MB check only exists in the web frontend booking-flow.tsx component.
Screenshot: In Postman, POST to /api/bookings/{id}/upload with a multipart file larger than 10MB. Capture HTTP 200 OK response with fileUrl field, demonstrating the oversized file was accepted.
7.2 BUG-02: Email Receipt Not Sent in Local Development Environment

After a successful PayMongo webhook triggers a payment confirmation, the booking status is correctly updated to PAID and the QR code is generated, but the email receipt is not delivered to the customer in the local development environment. No exception is thrown; the PaymentSucceededListener silently fails to send the email.
1. Trigger a PayMongo test webhook with a payment.paid event.
2. Verify booking status changes to PAID and QR code is stored.
3. Check the registered customer's email inbox — no receipt email is received.
4. Check backend logs — no SMTP error is printed.

Missing MAIL_USERNAME and MAIL_PASSWORD environment variables in the local .env file. This is a configuration issue, not a code defect. The feature works correctly in the deployed environment where these variables are set.
Note: This is an environment-specific issue and not a regression from the refactoring.
7.3 BUG-03: Mobile Booking Filter Chips Do Not Persist Selection State

In the MyBookingsFragment, the status filter chips (ALL, PENDING, PAID, DROPPED_OFF, PROCESSING, COMPLETED) do not visually persist their selected state after the RecyclerView refreshes or the user navigates away and back to the screen. While the filtering logic itself correctly filters the booking list, the selected chip reverts to 'ALL' after the list reloads, causing UI inconsistency.
1. Open the My Bookings screen in the Android app.
2. Tap the 'PAID' filter chip — list correctly shows only PAID bookings.
3. Pull down to refresh the list.
4. Observe that the 'ALL' chip is now highlighted again, but the list still shows only PAID bookings until the next scroll.

The chip selection state is stored in a local variable that is reset when the RecyclerView adapter notifies dataset changes. The selected filter status is not stored in the Fragment's ViewModel and is therefore lost on RecyclerView rebind.
8.1 FIX-01: Verified Application Context Loads After Refactoring

The vertical slice refactoring moved all classes to new packages. Any missed @ComponentScan path or broken @Autowired dependency would cause the Spring Application Context to fail to load, breaking the entire application.

After completing the package reorganization in PR #24, the contextLoads() integration test was re-executed and confirmed the Spring Boot Application Context initializes successfully with all beans wired correctly. All @Service, @Repository, @Controller, and @Component classes in the new features/ and shared/ packages are correctly discovered by Spring's component scan.
mvn test passes with zero failures. The LaundrylinkApplicationTests.contextLoads() test is the primary guard for this class of regression.
8.2 FIX-02: Frontend Route Paths Updated After Vertical Slice Reorganization
Import path regression from web refactoring
All web UI tests (SHOP-06 through OWNER-10)

Moving frontend components from src/components/ into features/<domain>/components/ changed all import paths. React Router page components in src/pages/ that imported from the old paths would have failed to resolve.

All import paths in src/pages/*.tsx were updated during the refactoring to point to the new features/<domain>/components/<ComponentName> paths. TypeScript's compiler (tsc) was used during the build step (npm run build) to catch any remaining broken imports at build time before deployment.
Running npm run build (tsc && vite build) completes with zero TypeScript errors. All page components render correctly in the browser.
8.3 FIX-03: Booking Overbooking Prevention Confirmed After Slot Service Relocation

The SlotService class, which enforces slot capacity by querying BookingRepository and SlotConfigRepository, was moved to the features/slot/ package. Since it depends on BookingRepository (in features/booking/), cross-feature dependencies had to remain intact. Any accidental removal of the inter-feature dependency injection would silently disable the overbooking check.

After the refactoring, manual testing confirmed that attempting to book a slot that has already reached its maxCapacity limit returns HTTP 409 Conflict with an appropriate error message. The @Autowired BookingRepository dependency in SlotService was verified to be preserved in the new package structure.
BOOK-04 passes. Attempting to create a second booking for the same shop, service, date, and time slot when the slot is full returns a 409 error response.
